text: The entry-candidate read is one operation, GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/entry-candidates?businessDate=&threshold=&page=&size=, published in the service's OpenAPI 3.1 document by this story because the split of RWB-E1-018 gives this slice no contract story. businessDate and threshold are required, page and size optional; the response is EntryCandidatePage with businessDate, threshold, asOf, page, size, total, candidates[] and breaks[]; a candidate carries accountKey, accountCode, productGroup, daysPastDue, totalBalance, contractNo, dataAsOf, tdrFlag, deceasedFlag, disputeOpen, deceasedOverride, bankruptcy and fraudFlag, with an absent extension row left absent; the identity is camelCase of the field it reads. The two extension writes are PUT /extension-facts/parties/{personKey} and PUT /extension-facts/accounts/{accountKey} with the flags of the row in the body. The status set is 400, 401, 403, 409 (the batch gate), 422 (a missing flag) and 503 (a view failure). The read is called by the service identity of the rwb-case case creation step and the writes by the exclusion screen through gateway-bff.
why: No source names an entry-candidate operation (TSD P1 v3 T-A.1 lists API-P1-001 to API-P1-016 without one; Architecture v5 slide 15 names the P1 IN paths and none of them is an entry read), the legacy read was an in-process interface with no path and no status code, and the split plan of RWB-E1-018 has no P1 contract story, so nothing else fixes the shape.

text: The entry read is one operation for a business date, executed as one statement set over the views and paged by page and size; the caller pages through the date and a per-account read is refused as a fan-out under the one-hop rule. The default page size and the maximum are fixed in the published contract of the read, and the case creation job of rwb-case reads the whole date in consecutive pages inside one execution rather than one hop per account.
why: The legacy job called CaseEntryService per account_key, DP-11 forbids a call chain and fixes one hop with a 2 s budget, and no source states the paging of a read that returns about 28,100 accounts at go-live.

The screen keeps the right, the confirmation and its audit; this service validates the caller's token and holds no role model. The party body carries vulnerable, deceasedOverride, bankruptcy and fraudFlag, so vulnerable is always written by the caller and never defaulted here; a repeat of the same body leaves one row, and a changed body replaces the flags on the same key with a version increment. An extension row is written for a key with no view row, is never refused for that reason, and the key is listed by REC-05 on the next read.
